suite: r1096 preparation duration, source, memory and queue regression
method: Shipped audio-preparation-r981.js in Node VM; own WAV and WebM/Opus fixtures exercise production container parsing; metadata/audio element, URL handling and decoded AudioBuffer results are controlled seams. No native browser decode, microphone capture or physical-device claim.

results.name: Published budgets remain 60 seconds, 8 MiB source, 32 MiB preparation
Valid two-second WAV reaches the controlled decode seam and releases its lease
WAV duration boundary is inclusive at 60 and typed duration rejection begins above 60
Valid WebM Opus fixture reaches production inspection and the controlled decode seam
WebM cluster timestamp accepts exactly 60 seconds and rejects an over-limit cluster before decode
WebM block timestamp raw boundary stays inclusive at 60 and rejects above 60 with the duration code
WebM block timestamps retain the conservative second: 59 seconds fits and 59.001 does not
WebM cumulative Opus samples accept exactly 60 seconds raw and reject the next packet before decode
WebM packet duration retains the conservative second: 59 seconds fits and one more packet does not
Over-8-MiB input is rejected without reading the source or calling decode
Thirty-second 48-kHz stereo source fits source limit but exceeds processing memory before decode
Malformed RIFF is a header error, independent of duration errors
Metadata-only format with unverifiable channel layout is a layout error before decode
Decoded duration and layout are independently checked after the controlled decode seam
Decoded-rate growth is re-budgeted and fails before use or output creation
Resident PCM counts toward the same budget and approved trimmers can reclaim it
Packed output headroom retains the active preparation estimate and resident URLs
Preparation queue serializes four admissions and rejects the fifth
Aborted decode rejects promptly but retains its lease until decode settles and blocks a new decode
Stale queued job is cancelled before decoding and does not disturb its predecessor
Controlled decoder failure releases the queue so a later preparation succeeds
